title: Docs: Performance profiles by hardware (H100/L40S/B200) + pinning/rollout caveats
author: Elliot Price
body:
Summary
Add internal/external draft doc page: “Performance profiles by hardware”. This is the customer-facing (and CS/Sales-supporting) slice of the hardware tuning profiles pack work landing with runtime-1.22.

Goals
- Provide a single place to understand what a “performance profile” is, how selection works by GPU SKU, and what customers can expect (and should watch) per SKU.
- Document expected behavior buckets (latency/throughput/memory tradeoffs) without over-promising exact numbers that are workload-dependent.
- Clarify what is supported/guaranteed in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, including profile version pinning and rollback guidance.

What’s included
- New page: Performance profiles by hardware
  - Definitions: profile_id vs profile_version, and why defaults may change across runtime releases.
  - Selection overview (high-level): auto-selected by detected GPU SKU + compatibility checks; Dedicated/Private can pin profile_version with guardrails.
  - “Expected behavior” tables for:
    - H100 (SXM/PCIe): best perf, widest stable concurrency; kernel variant behavior and fallback conditions.
    - L40S: cost-effective but tighter memory headroom; recommended concurrency caps; stability/OOM prevention notes.
    - B200 (Preview): explicitly labeled as early access; stricter compatibility gating; what metrics must be monitored.
  - Workload buckets referenced consistently with runtime docs:
    - Short prefill / short decode
    - Long prefill / short decode
    - Short prefill / long decode
    - Long context / mixed decode
  - Caveats:
    - Mixed workloads: p99 can regress if batching is too aggressive; we prioritize tail-latency stability over headline throughput.
    - Driver/CUDA variance: profiles include compatibility constraints; Private installs must meet stated baselines.
    - Quantization: throughput and memory characteristics differ; numbers are illustrative and not contractual.
  - Operational guidance:
    - How to tell what profile is active (Console/headers/debug endpoints; wording matches runtime-1.22 planned UX).
    - What to do if performance changes after upgrade: pin profile_version, confirm SKU detection, and check kernel fallback / queueing metrics.

Audience + publishing plan
- This PR is written to be publishable externally with minimal redaction. Anything fleet-specific (exact driver spread, instance mapping, internal SLO gates) is either excluded or phrased as “minimum supported baseline” / “contact support”.
- Internal callouts are marked with an “Internal note” admonition block and are safe to remove for external publishing.

Not included / follow-ups
- B200 tables are intentionally conservative and labeled Preview; we should update after ENG-4928 brings up more nodes.
- Console screenshots: placeholder callout referencing DES-214; we’ll add once UI lands.

Review checklist
- Product (Dedicated): ensure language matches PM-881 (what we disclose vs keep internal).
- SRE: ensure rollback/pinning guidance is safe and doesn’t conflict with Hosted kill-switch semantics.
- Observability: metric names and meanings match runtime profile dashboard spec.

Screenshots
- None (text-only).

conversation:
Lauren Bishop (review) — 2026-02-15
Please avoid giving the impression we guarantee specific tokens/sec in Dedicated. I like the buckets framing, but the table headers (“Typical throughput”) read like a promise. Suggest: “Observed range in Redwood benchmark lab (illustrative)” + explicit note that SLOs are latency/availability, not throughput.

Elliot Price (author) — 2026-02-15
Good call. Updated table caption + added a bold disclaimer in the “How to interpret the tables” section. Also tweaked Dedicated section to point to “capacity sizing guidance” rather than throughput guarantees.

Allison Grant (review) — 2026-02-16
Metric names: the page references scheduler.queue_ms and kernel.fallback_rate; we standardized on scheduler_queue_ms and runtime_kernel_fallback_total in the dashboard spec. Can we align here? Also please add a note on cardinality (profile_id label is safe; do not encourage per-customer tags).

Elliot Price (author) — 2026-02-16
Aligned metric names to the current spec and added a short “Metrics hygiene” paragraph under Troubleshooting.

Sean Gallagher (review) — 2026-02-17
Rollback/pinning guidance is mostly good. One concern: “pin profile_version during incident” should mention that Hosted customers cannot pin (support can mitigate via routing / fleet-level rollback). Dedicated can pin via support / contract. Private can pin via Helm.

Elliot Price (author) — 2026-02-17
Updated “Who can pin what” table with explicit Hosted limitations and the right escalation path.

Noah Patel (review) — 2026-02-18
Minor tech notes: H100 section says kernel variant v3 is default for long-context; please phrase as “preferred when eligible; otherwise fallback” to avoid implying we never fallback. Also add a short note that profile selection happens at runtime startup / model load.

Elliot Price (author) — 2026-02-18
Made the language conditional (“when eligible”) and added a 2-sentence selection overview.

Kira Thompson (review) — 2026-02-19
Support section: please include a concrete “what to send to support” checklist (active profile_version, SKU, driver, example request IDs). This matches INT-8831.

Elliot Price (author) — 2026-02-19
Added a checklist under “If you open a support ticket”.

Lauren Bishop (approval) — 2026-02-20
Approved with wording changes. Thanks for keeping this publishable.

Allison Grant (approval) — 2026-02-20
Approved.

Sean Gallagher (approval) — 2026-02-21
Approved. Rollout guidance looks safe now.
